votes.motion: Approve the LBA Consent agenda (setting public hearing dates of May 20 and June 3, 2025 for the Capital Projects Fund budget for Fiscal Year 2025-26)
votes.description: Sets public hearing dates for the Local Building Authority's Capital Projects Fund budget for FY2025-26, which covers bond debt service for the Glendale and Marmalade Libraries.

votes.motion: Adjourn as the LBA and convene as the City Council
votes.description: Closes the Local Building Authority meeting and transitions to the Salt Lake City Council meeting.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 17 of 2025 (Yalecrest-Upper Yale Local Historic District)
votes.description: Adopts an ordinance amending the zoning map to apply the H-Historic Overlay District, establishing the Yalecrest-Upper Yale Local Historic District covering 24 homes on Yale Avenue.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 18 of 2025 (Permitting Outdoor Theaters in Commercial Districts)
votes.description: Adopts an ordinance amending Title 21A to permit live performance theaters, indoor or outdoor, within the CG General Commercial District and other appropriate districts.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 19 of 2025 (Zoning Map Amendment at approximately 273 East 800 South), which includes the condition of a development agreement
votes.description: Adopts an ordinance rezoning the property at 273 East 800 South from Institutional to RMF-45 to enable a deeply affordable 34-unit housing project by First Step House, conditioned on a development agreement.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and defer action on the Alley Vacation near 1409 South Edison Street to a future Council meeting
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on the proposed alley vacation near 1409 South Edison Street and defers a final decision to a future meeting.

votes.motion: Continue the public hearing for Budget Amendment No. 5 for Fiscal Year 2024-25
votes.description: Continues the public hearing on Budget Amendment No. 5 for FY2024-25 to a future meeting date (May 6, 2025).

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and defer action on the Victim of Crime Act Grant (City Attorney Prosecutor's Office) to a future Council meeting
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on the VOCA grant application for the City Attorney Prosecutor's Office and defers action to a future consent agenda.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 10 of 2025 adopting the 2025-2029 Five-Year Consolidated Plan, including CDBG, ESG, HOME, and HOPWA funding, and approving an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement with HUD
votes.description: Approves the City's required five-year HUD Consolidated Plan for 2025-2029, establishing goals and funding priorities for four federal grant programs, along with an Interlocal Agreement with HUD.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 11 of 2025 adopting the 2025-2026 Annual Action Plan funding allocations (Exhibit A) for CDBG, ESG, HOME, and HOPWA – except for CDBG #5, the Housing Authority of Salt Lake City's Revitalizing Riverside Apartments project
votes.description: Approves the FY2025-26 HUD Annual Action Plan funding allocations of approximately $7.7 million for community service providers under CDBG, ESG, HOME, and HOPWA, excluding the Riverside Apartments item.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 11 of 2025 Annual Action Plan funding allocations for CDBG #5, the Housing Authority of Salt Lake City's Revitalizing Riverside Apartments project
votes.description: Approves the funding allocation for the Housing Authority of Salt Lake City's Revitalizing Riverside Apartments project under the FY2025-26 Annual Action Plan; Council Member Mano was recused due to his board membership with the Housing Authority.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 21 of 2025 approving a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between Salt Lake City and the Salt Lake City Police Association
votes.description: Approves an MOU between Salt Lake City and the Salt Lake City Police Association governing terms and conditions of employment for police officers.

votes.motion: Adopt a Legislative Action asking the Administration to review City code sections regarding the number of unrelated people living together in a dwelling unit and the definition of 'family' for recommendations on how to update
votes.description: Directs the Administration to review and provide recommendations for updating City code provisions related to the number of unrelated individuals allowed in a dwelling unit and the definition of 'family.'

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 20 of 2025 enacting temporary zoning regulations authorizing a temporary increase in overnight capacity at the Youth Homeless Resource Center at 888 South 400 West
votes.description: Enacts a temporary zoning regulation allowing the Volunteers of America Youth Resource Center to increase maximum overnight capacity up to 50 individuals, effective June 4, 2025, for up to 180 days.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 22 of 2025 enacting temporary zoning regulations authorizing a temporary increase in overnight capacity at the Geraldine E. King Women's Resource Center at approximately 131 East 700 South
votes.description: Extends a temporary zoning regulation allowing the Geraldine E. King Women's Resource Center to increase maximum overnight capacity up to 250 individuals, effective May 1, 2025, for up to 180 days.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 23 of 2025 enacting temporary zoning regulations authorizing a temporary increase in overnight capacity at the Gail Miller Resource Center at 242 West Paramount Avenue
votes.description: Extends a temporary zoning regulation allowing the Gail Miller Resource Center to increase maximum overnight capacity up to 250 individuals, effective May 1, 2025, for up to 180 days.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 24 of 2025 enacting temporary zoning regulations authorizing a temporary increase in overnight capacity at the St. Vincent de Paul Center at 437 West 200 South
votes.description: Extends a temporary zoning regulation allowing the St. Vincent de Paul Center to continue providing overnight homeless shelter accommodations beyond April 15, effective April 16, 2025, for up to 180 days.

votes.motion: Approve the City Council Consent agenda except Item 9 (Ari Tepper Transportation Advisory Board appointment), which required rescheduling to a future date
votes.description: Approves multiple consent items including setting FY2025-26 budget hearing dates, setting an alley vacation hearing date, approving Grant Holding Account Batch No. 4, and approving board appointments for Michelle Buhler, Wisam Khudhair, Sarah Foran, Kelbe Goupil, and Turner Bitton.
